newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: European Leisure says current trade up on 95.
newsitem.headline: European Leisure says current trade up on 95.

text.p: European Leisure Plc said on Tuesday that current trading was ahead of the same period last year and it was optimistic about future trading prospects.

Most of the improvement in current trading was due to amusement machine manufacturing business Maygay which was continuing to benefit from deregulation in the gaming sector, European Leisure said in its annual results statement.
"Within UK retail, the snooker business is also outperforming last year although turnover in the entertainments units has been at a similar level to previous years," the company said.
Pre-tax profits for the year to end-June 1996 were up 30 percent at 5.4 million stg, European Leisure said.

The snooker division performed strongly, with a substantial contribution from the introduction of American pool lounges, the company said. "Acquisition opportunities in this sector are being actively pursued," it said.
Maygay was also significantly ahead over the year, and growth was expected to continue, European Leisure said.

"As a result of deregulation there has been a strong growth in sales in the early part of the current financial year, though a quieter period is expected as the industry digests these recent changes," it said.
The company said there had been a weaker performance in its entertainments division due mainly to extreme weather conditions and the loss of income from sites during a development programme.
European Leisure said that in conjunction with its banking syndicate, it was considering normalising its capital and shareholder structure.

"It is intended that this will involve a placing of most of the banking syndicate's equity and the raising of new funds for the company primarily to take advantage of expansion opportunities," it said.
